rules.rule_description: Enable the cryptographic module self-checks mandated by the Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 140-3. The only correct way to switch the system to FIPS mode is to enable it during the RHEL installation.
rules.detection_step: Check FIPS mode status: cat /proc/sys/crypto/fips_enabled. A value of 1 indicates FIPS mode is enabled.
rules.remediation_step: Add fips=1 option to the kernel command line at the start of the system installation. On UEFI systems, press 'e' key and add fips=1 to the end of the linuxefi line. On BIOS systems, press Tab key and add fips=1 to the end of the kernel command line.

rules.rule_name: Configure FIPS Mode with RHEL Image Builder
rules.rule_description: Create a customized image with FIPS mode enabled using RHEL image builder by setting the fips directive in the blueprint.
rules.detection_step: After system boot, verify FIPS mode: cat /proc/sys/crypto/fips_enabled should return 1.
rules.remediation_step: Create a TOML blueprint file with [customizations] fips = true, then build the customized RHEL image using: image-builder build image-type --blueprint blueprint-name

rules.rule_description: Ensure the system-wide cryptographic policy is set to FIPS when operating in FIPS mode.
rules.detection_step: Check current cryptographic policy: update-crypto-policies --show. Should return 'FIPS'.
rules.remediation_step: Set FIPS cryptographic policy: update-crypto-policies --set FIPS. Note: Setting FIPS policy alone does not enable FIPS mode - system must be installed in FIPS mode.

rules.rule_description: Set appropriate system-wide cryptographic policy to ensure applications use secure cryptographic algorithms. Available policies: DEFAULT, LEGACY, FUTURE, and FIPS.
rules.detection_step: Display current policy: update-crypto-policies --show
rules.remediation_step: Set the desired policy: update-crypto-policies --set <POLICY>. Then reboot the system for changes to take effect.

rules.rule_name: Use FUTURE Cryptographic Policy for Enhanced Security
rules.rule_description: Apply stricter forward-looking security level intended for testing future policies. Disables SHA-1 in DNSSEC, rejects SHA2-224 and SHA3-224 hashes, disables 128-bit ciphers, requires minimum 3072-bit RSA/DH keys.
rules.detection_step: Check current policy: update-crypto-policies --show
rules.remediation_step: Set FUTURE policy: update-crypto-policies --set FUTURE && reboot. Note: May cause interoperability issues with public internet systems.

rules.rule_name: Configure Cryptographic Policies via Web Console
rules.rule_description: Set system-wide cryptographic policies using the RHEL web console graphical interface.
rules.detection_step: Log into RHEL web console and check Crypto policy value in Configuration card.
rules.remediation_step: In web console Overview page, click Crypto policy value, select desired policy in Change crypto policy dialog, click Apply and reboot.

rules.rule_description: Disable post-quantum cryptography algorithms by applying the NO-PQ subpolicy if required for compatibility reasons.
rules.detection_step: Check if PQC is enabled: update-crypto-policies --show. Look for NO-PQ suffix.
rules.remediation_step: Apply NO-PQ subpolicy: update-crypto-policies --set <POLICY>:NO-PQ. For example: update-crypto-policies --set DEFAULT:NO-PQ

rules.rule_name: Configure SSH Authentication with Smart Card
rules.rule_description: Configure OpenSSH to use SSH keys stored on a smart card for authentication, providing enhanced security through hardware-based key storage.
rules.detection_step: List keys from smart card: ssh-keygen -D pkcs11:
rules.remediation_step:
1. Generate keys on smart card and list them: ssh-keygen -D pkcs11: > keys.pub
2. Transfer public key to server: ssh-copy-id -f -i keys.pub user@server
3. Connect using smart card: ssh -i 'pkcs11:id=%01' server

rules.rule_name: Configure Apache with HSM-Protected Private Keys
rules.rule_description: Configure Apache HTTP server to use private keys stored on Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) through PKCS #11 for TLS encryption.
rules.detection_step: Check Apache SSL configuration files in /etc/httpd/conf.d/ssl.conf for PKCS #11 URIs.
rules.remediation_step:
Install pkcs11-provider package. In /etc/httpd/conf.d/ssl.conf, use PKCS #11 URIs:
SSLCertificateFile 'pkcs11:id=%01;token=softhsm;type=cert'
SSLCertificateKeyFile 'pkcs11:id=%01;token=softhsm;type=private?pin-value=111111'

rules.rule_description: Install OpenSCAP tools for configuration compliance scanning and vulnerability assessment against security baselines.
rules.detection_step: Verify packages are installed: rpm -q openscap-scanner scap-security-guide
rules.remediation_step: Install required packages: dnf install openscap-scanner scap-security-guide

rules.rule_description: Assess system configuration compliance against a specific security baseline using OpenSCAP.
rules.detection_step: List available profiles: oscap info /usr/share/xml/scap/ssg/content/ssg-rhel10-ds.xml
rules.remediation_step: Run compliance scan: oscap xccdf eval --report scan_report.html --profile <profile_ID> /usr/share/xml/scap/ssg/content/ssg-rhel10-ds.xml

rules.rule_name: Remediate System to Align with Security Baseline
rules.rule_description: Automatically remediate the system to align with a specific security baseline using OpenSCAP.
rules.detection_step: Review scan results to identify failed rules that require remediation.
rules.remediation_step: Run remediation: oscap xccdf eval --remediate --profile <profile_ID> --report remediation_report.html /usr/share/xml/scap/ssg/content/ssg-rhel10-ds.xml

rules.rule_description: Assess security compliance of containers or container images against security baselines using oscap-podman.
rules.detection_step: List container images: podman images. Get container ID: podman ps -a
rules.remediation_step: Scan container: oscap-podman <ID> xccdf eval --report scan_report.html --profile <profile_ID> /usr/share/xml/scap/ssg/content/ssg-rhel10-ds.xml

rules.rule_name: Create Custom Security Profile with Autotailor
rules.rule_description: Customize security profiles by modifying specific rules using the autotailor tool for organization-specific requirements.
rules.detection_step: Verify autotailor is installed: rpm -q scap-security-guide
rules.remediation_step: Use autotailor to create customized profile: autotailor --output <output_file> --profile <base_profile> <datastream>

rules.rule_description: Deploy the Keylime verifier component that performs initial and periodic checks of system integrity for monitored agents.
rules.detection_step: Check Keylime verifier service status: systemctl status keylime_verifier
rules.remediation_step:
1. Install: dnf install keylime-verifier
2. Configure IP in /etc/keylime/verifier.conf.d/
3. Open firewall: firewall-cmd --add-port 8881/tcp --permanent
4. Enable: systemctl enable --now keylime_verifier

rules.rule_description: Deploy the Keylime registrar component that maintains a database of all agents and hosts TPM vendor public keys.
rules.detection_step: Check Keylime registrar service status: systemctl status keylime_registrar
rules.remediation_step:
1. Install: dnf install keylime-registrar
2. Configure IP in /etc/keylime/registrar.conf.d/
3. Open firewall: firewall-cmd --add-port 8890/tcp --permanent
4. Enable: systemctl enable --now keylime_registrar

rules.rule_description: Deploy the Keylime agent on remote systems to be monitored for integrity by the verifier.
rules.detection_step: Check Keylime agent service status: systemctl status keylime_agent
rules.remediation_step:
1. Install: dnf install keylime-agent
2. Configure verifier and registrar IP in /etc/keylime/agent.conf.d/
3. Enable: systemctl enable --now keylime_agent

rules.rule_description: Configure Keylime for continuous runtime monitoring of file integrity on monitored systems.
rules.detection_step: Check agent configuration for allowlist and excludelist settings.
rules.remediation_step: Create allowlist with expected file hashes and configure in agent. Define excludelist for files that change frequently. Use keylime_tenant to provision agent with monitoring configuration.

rules.rule_description: Install Advanced Intrusion Detection Environment (AIDE) and initialize the file integrity database for intrusion detection.
rules.detection_step: Check AIDE package: rpm -q aide. Check database exists: ls -la /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz
rules.remediation_step:
1. Install: dnf install aide
2. Initialize database: aide --init
3. Activate database: mv /var/lib/aide/aide.db.new.gz /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz

rules.rule_description: Run AIDE integrity checks to detect unauthorized file modifications.
rules.detection_step: Run manual check: aide --check. Review output for any Changed, Added, or Removed entries.
rules.remediation_step:
Schedule regular checks via cron. Add to /etc/crontab:
05 4 * * * root /usr/sbin/aide --check

rules.rule_description: Update the AIDE database after legitimate system changes to prevent false positives.
rules.detection_step: Run check to identify changed files: aide --check
rules.remediation_step:
1. Update database: aide --update
2. Activate updated database: mv /var/lib/aide/aide.db.new.gz /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz

rules.rule_description: Deploy a Tang server for Network-Bound Disk Encryption to enable automated unlocking of LUKS-encrypted volumes.
rules.detection_step: Check Tang service: systemctl status tangd.socket
rules.remediation_step:
1. Install: dnf install tang
2. Enable service: systemctl enable tangd.socket --now
3. Verify: echo test | clevis encrypt tang '{"url":"http://tang.server:80"}' -y | clevis decrypt

rules.rule_name: Deploy Tang Server with Custom Port and SELinux
rules.rule_description: Deploy Tang server on a custom port with SELinux in enforcing mode.
rules.detection_step: Check Tang listening port: systemctl show tangd.socket -p Listen
rules.remediation_step:
1. Allow custom port: semanage port -a -t tangd_port_t -p tcp 7500
2. Open firewall: firewall-cmd --add-port=7500/tcp --permanent
3. Create override: systemctl edit tangd.socket with ListenStream=7500
4. Restart: systemctl restart tangd.socket

rules.rule_description: Configure Clevis client to automatically unlock LUKS-encrypted volumes using Tang server.
rules.detection_step: Check Clevis bindings: clevis luks list -d /dev/sda2
rules.remediation_step: Bind LUKS volume to Tang: clevis luks bind -d /dev/sda2 tang '{"url":"http://tang.server"}'

rules.rule_description: Configure automated unlocking of LUKS-encrypted volumes using TPM 2.0 policy.
rules.detection_step: Check TPM2 bindings: clevis luks list -d /dev/sda2
rules.remediation_step: Bind LUKS volume to TPM2: clevis luks bind -d /dev/sda2 tpm2 '{}'

rules.rule_description: Periodically rotate Tang server keys for security and update client bindings accordingly.
rules.detection_step: Check current keys: ls -la /var/db/tang/
rules.remediation_step:
1. Hide old keys: mv /var/db/tang/*.jwk /var/db/tang/.$(basename *.jwk)
2. Generate new keys: /usr/libexec/tangd-keygen /var/db/tang
3. Update clients: clevis luks regen -d /dev/sda2 -s 1

rules.rule_description: Deploy the fapolicyd framework to control application execution based on user-defined policies.
rules.detection_step: Check fapolicyd service: systemctl status fapolicyd
rules.remediation_step:
1. Install: dnf install fapolicyd
2. Enable: systemctl enable --now fapolicyd
3. Verify blocking: cp /bin/ls /tmp && /tmp/ls (should fail)

rules.rule_name: Mark Files as Trusted in fapolicyd
rules.rule_description: Mark custom files as trusted in fapolicyd to allow their execution.
rules.detection_step: Check trust database: fapolicyd-cli --list
rules.remediation_step:
Add trusted file: fapolicyd-cli --file add /path/to/binary --trust-file myapp
Update database: fapolicyd-cli --update

rules.rule_description: Add custom allow and deny rules to fapolicyd for specific application control.
rules.detection_step: List current rules: cat /etc/fapolicyd/compiled.rules
rules.remediation_step:
1. Create rule file in /etc/fapolicyd/rules.d/ with appropriate prefix number
2. Add rule: allow perm=execute all : trust=1
3. Update: fagenrules --load && systemctl restart fapolicyd

rules.rule_description: Enable integrity checking in fapolicyd to verify file integrity before allowing execution.
rules.detection_step: Check integrity setting in /etc/fapolicyd/fapolicyd.conf
rules.remediation_step:
Edit /etc/fapolicyd/fapolicyd.conf and set:
integrity = sha256 (for hash-based) or integrity = ima (for IMA-based)

rules.rule_description: Install USBGuard framework to protect against intrusive USB devices by controlling which devices can connect.
rules.detection_step: Check USBGuard service: systemctl status usbguard
rules.remediation_step:
1. Install: dnf install usbguard
2. Generate initial policy: usbguard generate-policy > /etc/usbguard/rules.conf
3. Enable: systemctl enable --now usbguard

rules.rule_description: Block specific USB devices from interacting with the system using USBGuard.
rules.detection_step: List USB devices: usbguard list-devices
rules.remediation_step:
Block device: usbguard block-device <ID>
Reject device permanently: usbguard reject-device <ID> -p

rules.rule_description: Authorize specific USB devices to interact with the system using USBGuard.
rules.detection_step: List blocked devices: usbguard list-devices | grep block
rules.remediation_step:
Temporarily allow: usbguard allow-device <ID>
Permanently allow: usbguard allow-device <ID> -p

rules.rule_description: Create custom USB device authorization policies for specific security requirements.
rules.detection_step: Review current rules: usbguard list-rules
rules.remediation_step:
1. Generate policy without hashes: usbguard generate-policy --no-hashes > ./rules.conf
2. Edit rules.conf with custom rules
3. Install: install -m 0600 -o root -g root rules.conf /etc/usbguard/rules.conf
4. Restart: systemctl restart usbguard

rules.rule_description: Configure IPC access control in USBGuard to limit which users can interact with the USBGuard service.
rules.detection_step: Check IPC settings: grep -E 'IPCAllowedUsers|IPCAllowedGroups|IPCAccessControlFiles' /etc/usbguard/usbguard-daemon.conf
rules.remediation_step:
Edit /etc/usbguard/usbguard-daemon.conf:
IPCAllowedUsers=username
or
IPCAllowedGroups=groupname
or use IPCAccessControlFiles option for file-based ACL

rules.rule_description: Configure USBGuard to log authorization events to the Linux Audit system.
rules.detection_step: Check audit logs for USBGuard events: ausearch -ts recent | grep -i usb
rules.remediation_step: Ensure AuditDebugEnabled option is set appropriately in /etc/usbguard/usbguard-daemon.conf. USBGuard logs to audit by default when audit daemon is running.

rules.rule_description: Deploy multiple Tang servers for high availability in NBDE deployments using Clevis SSS pin.
rules.detection_step: Check Clevis bindings for multiple Tang servers: clevis luks list -d /dev/sda2
rules.remediation_step:
Use SSS pin with multiple Tang servers:
clevis luks bind -d /dev/sda2 sss '{"t":1,"pins":{"tang":[{"url":"http://tang1"},{"url":"http://tang2"}]}}'

rules.rule_name: Remove Clevis Pin from LUKS Volume
rules.rule_description: Safely remove a Clevis pin binding from a LUKS-encrypted volume.
rules.detection_step: List current bindings: clevis luks list -d /dev/sda2
rules.remediation_step: Remove binding: clevis luks unbind -d /dev/sda2 -s <slot_number>

rules.rule_description: Configure Keylime for measured boot attestation to verify system state at boot time.
rules.detection_step: Check if measured boot is configured in Keylime agent settings.
rules.remediation_step: Enable measured boot in agent configuration. Configure verifier to validate boot measurements against expected values. Use keylime_tenant to provision with boot policy.

rules.rule_name: Use RHEL System Roles for AIDE Configuration
rules.rule_description: Use the aide RHEL system role to configure file integrity checks across multiple systems.
rules.detection_step: Verify ansible and rhel-system-roles packages are installed.
rules.remediation_step:
Create playbook using rhel-system-roles.aide:
- name: Configure AIDE
  hosts: all
  tasks:
    - include_role:
        name: rhel-system-roles.aide
      vars:
        aide_init: true
        aide_cron_check: true

rules.rule_name: Use RHEL System Roles for NBDE Configuration
rules.rule_description: Use nbde_server and nbde_client RHEL system roles to configure NBDE across multiple systems.
rules.detection_step: Verify ansible and rhel-system-roles packages are installed.
rules.remediation_step: Use nbde_server role for Tang servers and nbde_client role for Clevis clients in Ansible playbooks.

rules.rule_name: Use RHEL System Roles for fapolicyd Configuration
rules.rule_description: Use the fapolicyd RHEL system role to prevent users from executing untrustworthy code.
rules.detection_step: Verify ansible and rhel-system-roles packages are installed.
rules.remediation_step: Create playbook using rhel-system-roles.fapolicyd to configure application allowlisting across managed nodes.

rules.rule_name: Configure PKCS #11 PIN for LUKS Unlocking
rules.rule_description: Configure unlocking of LUKS-encrypted volumes using a PKCS #11 pin for hardware token-based authentication.
rules.detection_step: Check if PKCS #11 pin is configured: clevis luks list -d /dev/sda2
rules.remediation_step:
Bind LUKS volume to PKCS #11:
clevis luks bind -d /dev/sda2 pkcs11 '{"uri":"pkcs11:..."}'

rules.rule_name: Perform Hardened RHEL Installation with Kickstart
rules.rule_description: Perform a hardened installation of RHEL using Kickstart with a security profile applied automatically.
rules.detection_step: Review Kickstart file for oscap configuration.
rules.remediation_step:
Add to Kickstart file:
%addon org_fedora_oscap --profile=<profile_ID> --content-url=<url>
%end

rules.rule_name: Configure Automated LUKS Enrollment with Kickstart
rules.rule_description: Configure automated enrollment of LUKS-encrypted volumes during Kickstart installation using NBDE.
rules.detection_step: Review Kickstart file for Clevis configuration.
rules.remediation_step:
Add to Kickstart file:
%post
clevis luks bind -d /dev/sda2 tang '{"url":"http://tang.server"}' -y
%end

rules.rule_description: Identify and document applications using cryptography not compliant with FIPS 140-3.
rules.detection_step: Review list of non-FIPS compliant applications in RHEL documentation.
rules.remediation_step: Document exceptions for applications like: Bacula (CRAM-MD5), Cyrus SASL (SCRAM-SHA-1), curl (NTLM), MariaDB (mysql_native_password), Samba (RC4/DES for Windows interoperability). Consider alternatives or accept risk.

rules.rule_description: Create and set a custom system-wide cryptographic policy for specific organizational requirements.
rules.detection_step: List available policies: update-crypto-policies --list
rules.remediation_step:
1. Create policy file in /etc/crypto-policies/policies/
2. Define cryptographic settings in policy file
3. Apply: update-crypto-policies --set <custom_policy_name>
4. Reboot system

rules.rule_description: Customize system-wide cryptographic policies using subpolicies for fine-grained control.
rules.detection_step: Check current policy with subpolicies: update-crypto-policies --show
rules.remediation_step: Apply subpolicy: update-crypto-policies --set <POLICY>:<SUBPOLICY>. Example: update-crypto-policies --set DEFAULT:NO-SHA1

rules.rule_description: Create structured USBGuard policy by organizing rules in separate configuration files within /etc/usbguard/rules.d/.
rules.detection_step: List rule files: ls -la /etc/usbguard/rules.d/
rules.remediation_step:
1. Create separate .conf files in /etc/usbguard/rules.d/
2. Use numeric prefixes for ordering (e.g., 10-keyboards.conf)
3. Restart: systemctl restart usbguard

rules.rule_description: Deploy Tang server as a container for NBDE instead of RPM installation.
rules.detection_step: Check running container: podman ps | grep tang
rules.remediation_step:
Run Tang container:
podman run -d --name tang-server -p 80:80 -v /var/db/tang:/var/db/tang:Z registry.access.redhat.com/rhel9/tang
